subject: Enclave readiness and network constraints — post-demo notes
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Elise Novak <enovak@medforge.com>, Samir Choudhury <samir@medforge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Enclave readiness and network constraints — post-demo notes

Hi Elise / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Appreciate the clarity on the regulatory drivers and where the platform needs to fit in. Below is a quick summary of what we heard, open questions, and proposed next steps so we have alignment internally and with your infra team.

Summary of key pain points / goals
- Data residency: EU-only storage and processing for PHI-derived telemetry; no cross-border replication permitted.
- Air-gap intent: primary preference is an isolated enclave for inference with no outbound internet egress from the inference cluster.
- Network topology: plan to use private peering (ExpressRoute equivalent) to a DMZ hosted by your VPC team; no public load balancers.
- Audit & key management: HSM-backed keys preferred (FIPS-140-2/3); audit trail retention requirement = 7 years.
- Ops constraints: limited change windows and strict firewall rules; the team cannot open ephemeral ports for initial onboarding without change ticketing.

Technical clarifications / asks we have
1) Can you share a current network diagram (simple VPC segments + where dev/test vs prod will live) and the approved egress policy? This will help us size the private deployment and validate prefix-based rules.
2) Confirm whether outbound DNS resolution from the enclave is allowed via your internal resolver (we can work with stub-only DNS).
3) Do you have a preferred HSM vendor / KMS pattern we should integrate to for key wrapping?
4) Procurement path: who owns the security questionnaire and SLT approvals on your side (we want to engage early to reduce procurement lag).

Proposed next steps
- Please upload the network diagram and any egress policy PDF to the Drive link I shared (or reply to this thread).
- I'll schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive (Redwood infra + your network/security lead) — suggested slot: Thu 30 Jun, 10:00–11:00 CET.
- I'll attach a short deploy overview and our standard private deployment checklist for your infra team to review (see attachment).

Attachments referenced:
- enclave-demo-recording.mp4 (demo recording)
- redwood-deploy-overview.pdf (high-level private deployment steps)

If any of the summary items above are off the mark, call them out and I’ll correct. Otherwise we’ll proceed with the deep-dive scheduling and pre-call doc share.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

--
Redwood Inference — Production-first inference platform

Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 08:03:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Enclave readiness and network constraints — post-demo notes

Avery —

Thanks for the concise recap. Confirming the high-level items look right. A few clarifications and asks from our side:

1) Timeline: we’re targeting an internal Q4 approval window for a pilot (we need vendor security signoff + procurement). Can you provide a short statement of effort (SOE) for private deployment (hours for infra + typical handoff timeline)?
2) HSM: our security team prefers Thales Luna; we also have a cloud KMS option in the DR site we can discuss. Is Redwood able to integrate with a customer-provided HSM or do you have a recommended broker pattern?
3) Network: outbound internet is disallowed from the enclave except to a narrow set of internal IPs (for telemetry forwarding). We need to confirm whether Redwood requires any outbound endpoints for license checks / telemetry. If so, we’ll need the exact FQDN/IPs so our firewall team can assess.
4) Procurement: procurement will need your SOC2 report + a brief explanation of your data retention and deletion flows for customer-managed deployments. Please include those on the drive.

Samir and I are available for the deep-dive on Thu 30 Jun at 10:00 CET. Sending the network diagram and baseline egress policy after I sync with our infra lead this afternoon.

Elise
Dr. Elise Novak
VP, Engineering — MedForge Health
enovak@medforge.com | +44 20 7946 0999
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 16:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Enclave readiness and network constraints — post-demo notes

Elise / Samir —

Perfect, thanks for the confirmations. Quick answers and next artifacts we’ll provide: 

SOE / timeline: we’ll produce a 1–2 page SOE that covers estimated Redwood resource-days for an on-prem/private deployment (infra work, cert/key setup, testing window). Expect that by Tue 29 Jun EOD CET. Typical pilot path we see: 2–3 weeks to stage + 1 week to validate + ops hardening window; can compress depending on change-window availability.

HSM integration: Redwood supports customer-provided HSMs via PKCS#11 in our private deployments. We’ll include a short integration note for Thales Luna in the doc. If you have a managed KMS preference, we can map both patterns.

Outbound endpoints: Redwood’s runtime does not require persistent public egress for licensing. We do (optionally) use a small set of endpoints for crash telemetry and usage analytics in hosted flows; for private deployments these are off by default. If you opt-in to limited telemetry forwarding we’ll provide a precise IP/FQDN allowlist — otherwise no external egress required.

Procurement artifacts: attaching the deploy overview and we’ll upload SOC2 + retention note to the shared Drive.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Redwood: SOE + Thales integration note + upload SOC2 summary to Drive (Avery) — 2027-06-29 EOD CET
- MedForge: network diagram + egress policy + primary security contact (Elise) — 2027-06-28 EOD CET
- Schedule: hold 30 Jun 10:00 CET for tech deep-dive (calendar invite pending)

Attachments included: redwood-deploy-overview.pdf

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the SOE and the calendar invite.
